verses.text: "This is what you must do to set Aaron and his sons apart as holy, so that they can serve me as priests. Take a young bull and two rams with nothing wrong with them.
And from fine wheat flour, without yeast, make bread, thick loaves mixed with olive oil, and thin wafers brushed with olive oil.
Put them in a basket and bring them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
Take the clothes and dress Aaron in the shirt, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself, and the chest piece. Tie the woven belt of the ephod around him.
Put the turban on his head, and attach the holy crown to the turban.
Then take the anointing oil and anoint him by pouring it on his head.
Bring his sons and dress them in shirts.
Tie sashes on Aaron and his sons, and put caps on the sons. The priesthood will belong to them by a law that lasts forever. In this way you will ordain Aaron and his sons.
Bring the bull to the front of the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons are to put their hands on its head.
Kill the bull in front of the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
Take some of the bull's blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger. Pour out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar.
Then take all the fat around the insides, the best part of the liver, and both kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
But burn the bull's meat, its skin, and its dung outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons are to put their hands on its head.
Kill it, and take its blood and sprinkle it on all sides of the altar.
Cut the ram into pieces, and wash its insides and its legs. Put them with the pieces and the head.
Then burn the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a sweet smell, an offering made to the LORD by fire.
Take the other ram, and Aaron and his sons are to put their hands on its head.

Kill it, and take some of its blood and put it on the bottom of the right ears of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then sprinkle the rest of the blood on all sides of the altar.

Take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes. Then he and his sons and their clothes will be made holy.
Take the fat from this ram, the fat tail, the fat around the insides, the best part of the liver, both kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh. This is the ram for the ordination.
From the basket of bread made without yeast, which is in front of the LORD, take one loaf of bread, one thick loaf made with oil, and one thin wafer.
Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and have them lift them up in front of the LORD as a wave offering.
Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar on top of the burnt offering, as a sweet smell to the LORD. It is an offering made to the LORD by fire.
Take the breast of the ram for Aaron's ordination, and lift it up in front of the LORD as a wave offering. It will be your share.
Set apart as holy the parts of the ram for the ordination that belong to Aaron and his sons: the breast that was waved and the thigh that was lifted up.
This is always to be the share that Aaron and his sons receive from the people of Israel. It is the gift the people of Israel must give to the LORD from their peace offerings.
Aaron's holy clothes will belong to his descendants after him, so that they can be anointed and ordained in them.
The son who becomes priest after him, and comes into the Tent of Meeting to serve in the Holy Place, is to wear them for seven days.
Take the ram for the ordination and boil its meat in a holy place.
At the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons are to eat the meat of the ram and the bread in the basket.
They are to eat these offerings by which their sins were covered when they were ordained and made holy. No one else may eat them, because they are holy.
If any of the meat of the ordination or any of the bread is left until morning, burn it. It must not be eaten, because it is holy.
Do all this for Aaron and his sons, just as I have commanded you. Take seven days to ordain them.
Every day offer a bull as a sin offering to cover sin. Make the altar clean by offering a sacrifice for it, and anoint it to make it holy.
For seven days make the altar clean and set it apart as holy. Then the altar will be most holy, and whatever touches it will be holy.
This is what you are to offer on the altar every day, without fail: two lambs a year old.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other in the evening.
With the first lamb offer about a kilogram and a half of fine flour mixed with about one litre of oil from pressed olives, and about one litre of wine as a drink offering.
Offer the other lamb in the evening, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning. It is a sweet smell, an offering made to the LORD by fire.
For all generations to come, this burnt offering is to be made every day at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting in front of the LORD. There I will meet you and speak to you.
There I will also meet with the people of Israel, and the place will be made holy by my glory.
I will make the Tent of Meeting and the altar holy. And I will set apart Aaron and his sons as holy to serve me as priests.
Then I will live among the people of Israel and be their God.
They will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of Egypt so that I could live among them. I am the LORD their God."
